subsystems.name: Hybrid nanowire
subsystems.role: hosts the Majorana modes at its ends, where information would be stored non-locally.
parts: indium arsenide or indium antimonide semiconductor nanowire

subsystems.name: Gate electrodes
subsystems.role: tune the electrostatic potential along the nanowire to create and move Majorana modes.

subsystems.name: Cryogenic and magnetic environment
subsystems.role: provides the millikelvin temperatures and magnetic field needed for the topological phase.

subsystems.name: Braiding control
subsystems.role: moves Majorana modes around each other so their exchange performs a quantum operation.

subsystems.name: Readout
subsystems.role: measures the parity of a pair of Majorana modes without destroying the encoded information.

buildSteps.title: Grow semiconductor nanowires
buildSteps.detail: crystal growth (e.g. metal-organic vapour phase epitaxy) produces nanowires with atomically clean facets.

buildSteps.title: Deposit the superconductor
buildSteps.detail: aluminium is grown epitaxially on the nanowire facets to form a clean semiconductor–superconductor interface.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the device
buildSteps.detail: nanowires are placed on a substrate, then gate electrodes and ohmic contacts are patterned by lithography.

buildSteps.title: Cool and apply a field
buildSteps.detail: the chip is cooled in a dilution refrigerator to a few thousandths of a kelvin and a magnetic field is applied along the nanowire.

buildSteps.title: Tune into the topological regime
buildSteps.detail: gate voltages are adjusted so the nanowire enters a topological phase, signalled by a zero-bias conductance peak.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate braiding
buildSteps.detail: voltage pulses move Majorana modes along the nanowire and exchange their positions, testing for non-Abelian statistics.

buildSteps.title: Form a qubit
buildSteps.detail: two or more Majorana pairs are coupled so that braiding implements logical operations, with readout of the pair parity.

buildSteps.title: Scale and error-correct
buildSteps.detail: many nanowires are integrated into arrays and operated under a topological error-correction scheme.

prerequisites.why: clean, epitaxial interfaces are needed to host robust Majorana modes and are demonstrated only in small devices.
zero-bias conductance peaks have been reported, but their interpretation as Majorana modes remains debated.
the exchange of quasiparticles has not yet been unambiguously demonstrated in any experiment.
dilution refrigerators and advanced lithography are widely available for quantum device research.
mathematical schemes exist to compute with braided anyons, but they have not been tested in hardware.

pathway.milestone: controlled nanowire devices showing zero-bias peaks and tunable hybridisation
pathway.unlocks: better understanding of the materials and signatures.

pathway.milestone: unambiguous demonstration of non-Abelian statistics through braiding
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the quasiparticles can encode quantum information.

pathway.milestone: a single topological qubit with braiding-based operations and readout
pathway.unlocks: a hardware platform with intrinsic noise protection.

pathway.milestone: scalable arrays of topological qubits under error correction
pathway.unlocks: fault-tolerant quantum computing if the physics holds at scale.
